newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Suez okay on Tractebel-Electrabel merger - paper.
newsitem.headline: Suez okay on Tractebel-Electrabel merger - paper.

text.p: French Compagnie de Suez is not opposed to a merger between Belgian energy holding company Tractebel and its electricity unit Electrabel, Belgian financial daily De Financieel-Economische Tijd said on Wednesday.

The paper said Suez chairman Gerard Mestrallet had approved the merger in writing. A joining-up of the two would dispel fears over the impact of the merger between Suez and French utility group Lyonnaise des Eaux on Tractebel.
A Tractebel-Electrabel merger would safeguard Tractebel's operational autonomy and thus Belgian interests, the paper said.
Such a merger would further bolster Tractebel, which is already getting a boost from a full merger with Powerfin, the subsidiary managing its overseas interests.

The paper said Tractebel would hold 42 percent in Electrabel, which has a virtual monopoly in the Belgian power market, after the Powerfin merger. Tractebel has a bourse capitalisation of 213 billion francs, Electrabel one of 442 billion francs.
A merger would cut the interest of Belgian holding company Societe Generale de Belgique SA (SGB) in Tractebel to 25 percent from 50 percent after the Tractebel-Powerfin deal.
Societe Generale, controlled by Suez, had 65 percent before the Tractebel-Powerfin merger.

The paper said Mestrallet's approval did not mean the Tractebel-Electrabel merger would be carried out instantly. It did, however, signify that preparations were underway and that the ball was now in the court of Tractebel's management.
